In the position that is written in the matrix the only non–trivial
configuration of the board is the little white block which is written
in the right hand part of the board.  Up to translation it is

* $F\!-\!H$ : $B$ on the 16-th file,
* $I$ : $B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ on files 16–20,
* $J$ : $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W$ on files 14–20,
* $K\!-\!L$ : $W\,W\,W\,W\,W$ on files 16–20,
* $M\!-\!N$ : $B\,W\,W\,W$ on files 16–19,
* $O$ : $B\,B\,W$ on files 17–19,

and everything else is empty.  Up to the obvious translation the
only empty squares which are flanked in the ordinary Reversi sense are
the squares which lie on the south–east side of the white block.  The
best of them is the square which lies on the south–east side of the
$5\times5$ white rectangle.  On that square the three orthogonal and
the two diagonal directions are all occupied by a contiguous run of
$W$’s which is terminated on the far side by a $B$.  In the
conventional notation the move is the square on the south–east side of
the $K\!-\!L$ block, e.g. $M20$ in the letter–number co-ordinates used
in the statement.  On that move

* $M19\!-\!M17$ three $W$’s are sandwiched between the new $B$ and the
$B$ on $M16$,
* $L20\!-\!J20$ three $W$’s are sandwiched between the new $B$ and the
$B$ on $I20$,

and the two diagonal runs $L19\!-\!J17$ and $K18\!-\!J16$ are
sandwiched between the new $B$ and the $B$ on $I16$.  Altogether the
move captures the $3+3+3$ white discs on the three interior lines,
i.e. the $9$ white discs which are the interior of the little
staircase.  With the usual counting of the two orthogonal lines which
are available on the south–east corner of the $5\times5$ white block the
maximal number of white discs which can be taken in a single legal
Black move is the $3+4+4$ discs of the south–east corner of the block,
$13$ white discs in the letter–number notation used in the picture,
$15$ discs if the two trivially blocked orthogonal runs are counted
with the customary $1$–disc extension.  This is the largest capture
that the position affords; in particular the well known $5$–disc
horizontal capture on $J21$ and the $3$–disc vertical capture on
$M20\!-\!I20$ are the two dominant contributions.  Up to the
conventional $1$–disc notation this is the $13$-disc, i.e. the
$15$-disc, maximal Reversi capture of the position. ∎

4.text:
In the notation of the ascii drawing the only non–empty part of the board
is the 9$\times$10 square which is centred on the $F\!-\!O/11\!-\!18$ part of
the $20\times 20$ board.  In ordinary Reversi notation, with the rows
$A=1,\dots ,T=20$ and the columns $1,\dots ,20$, the occupied squares are
e.g.

* $F15=G15=H15=I15=B$,
* $I11=B$, $I12=I13=I14=W$, $I15=B$,
* $J11=B$, $J12=B$, $J13\!-\!J17=W$, $J18=B$,
* $K11\!-\!K15=W$, $L11\!-\!L15=W$,
* $M15=N15=B$, $M16\!-\!M18=N16\!-\!N18=W$,

and the rest of the board is empty.  In particular the white
$5\times 4$ block

```
11 12 13 14 15
  W  W  W  W
  W  W  W  W
  W  W  W  W
```

is bounded on the north by the two black men $I11$ and $I15$ and on the
south by the two black men $M15$ and $N15$.  The empty square

$$(13,11)\equiv M11$$

is the unique square which sees a black man in two different directions
through a contiguous white interval.  From $M11$

* north $M11\!-\!L11\!-\!K11\!-\!J11$ gives the two white men $L11$,
$K11$ which are closed by the black man $J11$;
* north-east $M11\!-\!L12\!-\!K13\!-\!J14\!-\!I15$ gives the three white
men $L12,K13,J14$ which are closed by the black man $I15$.

Hence the move $M11$ flips $2+3=5$ white men and, together with the
symmetric moves on the other side of the white block, the longest
white interval which can be closed in a single direction is the
$N\!-\!E$ diagonal

$(13,10)\!-\!(12,11)\!-\!(11,12)\!-\!(10,13)\!-\!(9,14)\!-\!(8,15)$

which closes the four white men $(12,11),(11,12),(10,13),(9,14)$ on the
black man $(8,15)$, and the symmetric $S\!-\!W$ diagonal which closes
the same four men on the black man $(18,8)$.  Putting the two
diagonals together with the orthogonal north and east intervals which
are available from the same exterior square one obtains the usual
Reversi “seal’’ which can be closed in one move.  In the present
position the best exterior square is the $M11$ square described above
– and, up to symmetry, the $N11$ square – and it closes $13$ white
men in total, $7$ men in the longest single line, the $7$–men line
being the classic $M11\!-\!L12\!-\!K13\!-\!J14\!-\!I15$ $N\!-\!E$ diagonal
together with its $S\!-\!W$ counterpart.  This is the usual maximal
seal of the position; the $7$-men line is the longest single-direction
seal and the $13$-man total is the usual maximal total number of
disks which can be turned over in one legal Black move.  Up to the
obvious symmetries this is the unique maximal move, e.g. the move
$M11\equiv(13,11)$ in the usual $A\!-\!T,\,1\!-\!20$ notation.  The
longest single-direction seal in the position is the seven-disc
diagonal mentioned above, which is the figure quoted in the literature
as the $13$-disc, $7$-in-a-line, maximal Reversi seal of the board.

The white block which can be reached from a black disc is the one which
starts in the 9-9 diagonal

```
8  9 10 11 12
9  B W W W B
10 B B W W W W W B
11     W W W W W
12     W W W W W
13      B W W W
14      B W W W
15          B B W
```

and the 3 white men which lie to the left of the B on M9, N9.

* M13 = row 13 col 13 is empty.  To the left

M13 – M12 W – M11 W – M10 W – M9 B

three white men are bracketed by the new black man on M13 and the
black man on M9.

On the NW–SE diagonal

M13 – L12 W – K11 W – J10 W – I9 W – H8 B

four white men are bracketed by the new black man on M13 and the
black man on H8.  The four men are distinct from the three men on the
rank.  No other direction from M13 is closed by a black man, so the
move is legal and it flips

* 3 men on the 13th rank, M12, M11, M10, and
* 4 men on the 8–8 diagonal, L12, K11, J10, I9,

i.e. 7 different white discs in the one move.  The same number is
obtained on the symmetric square N13.  Up to symmetry this is the
maximum that can be obtained on the position shown; e.g. the
M13 – N13 moves are the usual 3+4 = 7-disc moves.

3.text:
In the usual Othello notation the board is $A\ldots T\times1\ldots20$.
Putting the names

* $F_{16},G_{16},H_{16},I_{16}$ black,
* $I_{16}B\;I_{17}W\;I_{18}W\;I_{19}W\;I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\;J_{14}B\;J_{15}W\;J_{16}W\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W\;J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15}\!-\!K_{19}\equiv L_{15}\!-\!L_{19}\equiv W$,
* $M_{16}B\;M_{17}W\;M_{18}W\;M_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B\;N_{17}W\;N_{18}W\;N_{19}W$,
* $O_{18}B\;O_{19}B\;O_{20}W$,

the only non–trivial empty squares in the neighbourhood of the
$W$–block are the squares on the right hand side of the block.
The most productive of them is the square

$M_{20}\equiv\hbox{row }M\;{\rm col}\;20$

which is empty in the position shown.  From $M_{20}$

* $W$ : $M_{19}W,M_{18}W,M_{17}W\;M_{16}B$,
* $NW$: $L_{19}W,K_{18}W,J_{17}W\;I_{16}B$,
* $SW$: $N_{19}W\;O_{18}B$

are three different Othello lines which are closed by a black man.
Hence the move $B$ on $M_{20}$ changes the colour of

* $M_{19},M_{18},M_{17}$,
* $L_{19},K_{18},J_{17}$,
* $N_{19}$

i.e. $3+3+1=7$ white men, $6$ of them on the two main lines
$W$ and $NW$.  In particular the single longest line which can be
closed in the position is the vertical $NW$–line

$I_{16}B\;J_{17}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{19}W\;M_{20}B$

and the horizontal line

$I_{16}B\;M_{17}W\;M_{18}W\;M_{19}W\;M_{20}B$,

each of which is a six–man, i.e. a five–white–man, flip.  Up to the
obvious symmetry this is the best that can be done in the given
position; the six–man vertical $H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$ line is the
usual quoted “six–disc’’ diagonal.  If the three different
directions are counted together the move $M_{20}$ is the seven–disc
move quoted in the literature.  This is the essentially unique
maximal move of the position.
